t: Item 175 in the analysis of chapter 7 of title 28 of the United States Code, immediately preceding section 171, is amended to read as follows: “175. Assignment of judges; divisions; hearings; quorum: decisions.”

fable.w: This section is a clerical amendment to the table of contents (analysis) of chapter 7 of title 28, changing the caption of item 175. The tempting reading is that the word "hearings" signals a public hearing, but it only appears in a heading about the internal organization of a court (assignment of judges, quorum, decisions). No outside party is consulted or given a right to sue over or take part in any federal decision.
fable.s: “175. Assignment of judges; divisions; hearings; quorum: decisions.”

qwen_block.w: This section merely amends a table of contents or analysis header for a chapter of the U.S. Code. It does not establish any process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The mention of 'hearings' refers to judicial proceedings within the federal court system, not public participation in administrative decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Item 175 in the analysis of chapter 7 of title 28 of the United States Code, immediately preceding section 171, is amended to read as follows: “175. Assignment of judges; divisions; hearings; quorum: decisions.”

opus.w: This provision only changes the wording of a table-of-contents entry for a section of title 28. It creates no public hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue. The word "hearings" is just part of a section heading, so it is a keyword match with no outside-party process behind it.
opus.s: “175. Assignment of judges; divisions; hearings; quorum: decisions.”
opus.b: 1. The tempting reading is "Yes," because the amended heading includes the word "hearings." That reading fails. The text only rewrites a table-of-contents entry in title 28 about the Court of Claims. It sets up no hearing before a federal decision, and it involves no one outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a table of contents or index for Title 28 of the U.S. Code. It does not establish any process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The mention of 'hearings' refers to judicial proceedings, which are not considered participation under the definition provided.
qwen_chat.s: Item 175 in the analysis of chapter 7 of title 28 of the United States Code, immediately preceding section 171, is amended to read as follows: “175. Assignment of judges; divisions; hearings; quorum: decisions.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that "hearings" implies public participation. However, in the context of judicial administration (Title 28), "hearings" refers to court proceedings or internal judicial administrative hearings, not public comment periods or advisory committees involving outside parties. Furthermore, this section is merely an amendment to a table of contents or index ("Item 175 in the analysis... is amended to read as follows"), not a substantive grant of participatory rights.
